The '''Hirabaru Site''' (平原遺跡) is a {{ill|Yayoi period|en|Yayoi period|qid=Q207858|lt=Yayoi period|1=Yayoi period}} archaeological site located in [[Itoshima City]], {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|qid=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}}. It is part of the [[Sone Archaeological Sites|Sone Archaeological Site Group]] and was designated a [[National Historic Site of Japan]] in 1982, with an additional designation in 2000.
== Overview ==
[[File:Hirabaru Site, tomb-1.jpg|thumb|250px|Hirabaru Site - Tomb 1]]
[[File:Hirabaru Site Relics, Distorted Naiōka Mon Yōyōkyō (Replica).JPG|thumb|250px|Distorted Naiōka Flower Eight-Petal Mirror (Replica)<br>{{small|Exhibited at the Ito-koku History Museum.}}]]
The Hirabaru Site consists of five Kofuns dated to the late {{ill|Yayoi period|en|Yayoi period|qid=Q207858|lt=Yayoi period|1=Yayoi period}} to the final Yayoi period. Tomb 1 was discovered accidentally in January 1965 during the development of a mandarin orange orchard, leading to an academic excavation led by [[Daihachi Harada]]. Subsequent investigations between 1988 and 1999 revealed five Kofuns in total. Today, only Tomb 1 has been restored and preserved as part of the "Hirabaru Historical Park."
Tomb 1 yielded numerous artifacts, including 40 mirrors—five of which are 46.5 cm in diameter—making it a significant discovery. All artifacts are designated as the {{ill|National Treasure (Japan)|en|National Treasure (Japan)|qid=Q1139795|lt=National Treasure (Japan)|1=National Treasure (Japan)}} under the title "Artifacts Excavated from the Hirabaru Rectangular Moated Burial Site in Fukuoka Prefecture" and are housed at the [[Ito-koku History Museum]].
== Details ==
Tomb 1 is a [[rectangular moated tomb]] containing a [[split-log coffin]]. Among its grave goods, numerous fragments of Japanese- and Chinese-made [[:en:Bronze mirrors|Bronze mirrors]] were discovered and reconstructed into 39 complete pieces.
A material analysis during its designation as an {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property (Japan)|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} in 1990 suggested that fragments previously attributed to four large mirrors with a diameter of 46.5 cm actually represented five distinct mirrors. These mirrors, known as "Large Naiōka Flower Mirrors," are exhibited at the {{ill|Kyushu National Museum|en|Kyushu National Museum|qid=Q148543|lt=Kyushu National Museum|1=Kyushu National Museum}} (one piece) and the Ito-koku History Museum (four pieces). The count of 40 mirrors makes this the largest number of bronze mirrors ever discovered in a single tomb in Japan (as of 2009).
The Large Naiōka Flower Mirror, with a diameter of 46.5 cm, matches the dimensions of the [[:en:Yata-no-Kagami|Yata-no-Kagami]], as its circumference equals eight "yata" units of measurement.
Harada reported that the bronze mirror fragments were not deliberately broken.<ref>Harada, "Hirabaru Yayoi Kofun: The Tomb of Ōhirume," p. 24.</ref>
== Main Artifacts ==
;Tomb 1
* [[Large Naiōka Flower Mirror]] - 5 pieces (or 4), also called "Naiōka Eight-Petal Mirror"<ref group="Note">The mirrors have only four knobs (central parts), and only two mirrors and two-thirds can be completely restored. This led Harada to conclude that the Naiōka Eight-Petal Mirror comprised four pieces.</ref>, made in Japan, with a diameter of 46.5 cm.
* Naiōka Flower Mirrors - 2 pieces
* [[Fang-kuei-chi (Chinese square grid pattern mirrors)]] - 32 pieces
* Sōji Mon Mirror - 1 piece
* Agate Tubular Beads (12 pieces), Glass Magatama (3 pieces), Glass Spheres (a11rox. 500), Small Glass Beads (a11rox. 500), Glass Tubular Beads (a11rox. 30), Glass Chains (a11rox. 900)
* Earrings (3 fragments)
* Iron Sword with Plain Ring Pommel (1)
The designated National Treasure items are as follows:<ref name="mon74">Notification No. 74 by the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science, and Technology, 2006.</ref>
* "Artifacts Excavated from the Hirabaru Rectangular Moated Burial Site in Fukuoka Prefecture"
''' Bronze Mirrors - 40 pieces
''' Ornaments - one set
''' Iron Sword with Plain Ring Pommel - 1
''' Accompanying items: pottery fragments, small glass beads, iron arrowheads, etc.
== Considerations ==
Harada identified the Large Naiōka Flower Mirror as the Yata-no-Kagami and proposed that the [[Ise Grand Shrine]]'s mirror was originally of this type.<ref name="jituzai">Harada, "Actual Myths," 1966.</ref> A passage in the [[Shintō Gobusho|Shinto Gobusho]] describes the Yata-no-Kagami as "八頭花崎八葉形也" (a shape with eight petals). The Large Naiōka Flower Mirror is the only archaeological artifact matching this description.
== Location ==
Hirabaru Historical Park, Hirabaru, Itoshima City, Fukuoka Prefecture
== Festivals ==
Each October 20th, the local "Terutomi Shrine" in [[Naka City]] holds the "Ōhirume Spirit Festival," inspired by Harada's theories. The Hirabaru Tomb Festival is held by the local community in mid to late October.
== Access ==
Take the [[Itoshima Community Bus]] (Sone Ground Line) from JR {{ill|Chikuzen-Maebaru Station|en|Chikuzen-Maebaru Station|qid=Q898453|lt=Chikuzen-Maebaru Station|1=Chikuzen-Maebaru Station}} or {{ill|Hatae Station|en|Hatae Station|qid=Q5367252|lt=Hatae Station|1=Hatae Station}} and alight at "Hirabaru Kofun Entrance." The site is a two-minute walk from the bus stop.
